comment: Several things struck me: There is still a need to be clear on what essential is for countries (bare minimum and country specific) and negotiating the expectation within DDA that REDDHI is one mechanism to bring our different projects together under one chapeau (‘the kitchen sink of what’s on the menu’); A possible country menu approach is one way of being country driven and responding to county priorities, but again this needs to be focused on core elements of REDDHI As we try and ‘retrofit’ the second D into the original REDHI it will need some rethinking graphically so the data and digital elements are more of  a continuum or at least together (I know you tried this previously with the patient journey which worked well and some of the other graphics but need to balance the person centred approach with the systems perspective) – I will ask Wendy to take a stab at this as she was suggesting this and see what we come up with next week. Balancing PHC and AI expectations / outcomes through more than word smithing  requires much more dialogue there are five remaining issues I think worth discussing further Defining ‘essential’ REDDHI financial and technical needs?: On one hand, the current version expanded beyond the original concept and it’s like ‘apple pie’ that nobody can say no to! (as we have more inputs and try and retrofit data aspects), to potentially include ‘too broad’ a range of data and digital health norms & standards, and we need to focus on REDDHI being a state and what is ‘essential’ for countries; One the other hand, each country is different and maybe we (WHO) need to offer  a ‘range of options’ for norms / standards to address their country  priorities and what countries see as ‘essential’ and ‘investable’ in. Perhaps countries need to define what is essential for them and not us – but selection from a range of norms and standards? Country ownership, country driven and resilient financing: In addition to technical data and digital health norms and standards, we need to look at structures within Govt planning and financing cycles & processes (to ensure MoF and key banks are included in broader planning and budgeting processes for laying foundations within, and beyond, the health sector) These Govt. ‘structures’ are also important for a) data and digital sovereignty, b) national legal agreements on sharing and financing and c) accountability and oversight. Perhaps we need to map out country planning cycles and existing coordination structures that include departments of planning and financing, NSOs and partnership coordination mechanisms Ensuring data standards are incorporated (but don’t delay / disrupt digital health DPI work to date): The list of data standards to be considered is on slide 7 – surveys needs further discussion on whether they are included or not; Modernization country-facing data analytics package needs further clarity but lies at heart of HMIS capacity and ability to analyze data for action; Front line health worker perspective still missing HMIS (slide put together to consider  - ‘two sides of one coin’ i) person centred journey with need for personalized approaches and ii) systems view point for digital and data – what the Govt system needs to have secure, trusted quality data to make decisions REDDHI as a way of uniting tools / projects  / a chapeau for DDA resource mobilization? It may be too broad, and everyone may need to see ‘their’ project in it, but some mentioned REDDHI (as concept & goal), with a robust ToC, could drive pulling together of tools / assessments / approaches for norms & standards for DDA  when we approach donors / funders for our work (continuum of data / digital / AI); Norms and standards are highlighted in slide 7 i ) survey or not and ii) assessment / maturity tools to provide basis of country maturity ready for assessment (or not eg. SCORE / MONITOR) Being more driven by country needs and showing impact: Appetite of REDDHI concept to be used as ‘menu’ of WHO norms and standards and potential structures to be supported to get to ‘REDDHI state’ / health goals – leaves countries more in driver’s seat to pick and choose what they need; Obv. needs series of regional office sensitization and RO’s driving country selection and coordinating support, together with HQ WG as part of work plan – needs to happen soon.
